1.title: LORE knowledge mode — standard-text consensus (not source-verified) (tier K)

2.title: LORE knowledge mode — exam convention (PYQ keys) (tier K)

K1.text: Breast cancer is the **most common cancer in women** in India and worldwide.

K2.text: The **upper outer quadrant** is the most common site, because it holds the most breast tissue (including the axillary tail of Spence).

K3.text: **Invasive ductal carcinoma, no special type (NST)** is the most common histological type, forming about 70–80% of cases.

K4.text: **BRCA1** lies on chromosome **17q** and **BRCA2** on chromosome **13q**; BRCA2 is the one more associated with **male** breast cancer.

K5.text: **Triple assessment** = clinical examination + imaging (mammography and/or ultrasound) + tissue diagnosis (**core needle biopsy** preferred over FNAC).

K6.text: **Axillary lymph node status** is the single most important prognostic factor.

K7.text: **Peau d'orange** is caused by obstruction of the subdermal (cutaneous) lymphatics with skin oedema, and puts the tumour in **T4b**.

K8.text: **Inflammatory carcinoma (T4d)** is due to tumour emboli in dermal lymphatics, and is treated with **neoadjuvant chemotherapy → modified radical mastectomy → radiotherapy**, never breast-conserving surgery.

K9.text: **Ipsilateral supraclavicular** node involvement is **N3c**, not M1, in current AJCC staging.

K10.text: **Tamoxifen** is the hormonal agent for ER-positive **premenopausal** women; **aromatase inhibitors** (letrozole, anastrozole, exemestane) are preferred in **postmenopausal** women.

K11.text: **Trastuzumab** targets HER2 and its key toxicity is **cardiotoxicity** (usually reversible, not dose-dependent).

K12.text: The **intercostobrachial nerve** is the nerve most often injured/sacrificed in axillary dissection, giving numbness of the medial upper arm; injury to the **long thoracic nerve** gives **winging of the scapula**.

K13.text: Carcinoma breast is a malignant tumour arising from the epithelium of the terminal duct–lobular unit of the breast.

K14.text: It is **in situ** (DCIS, LCIS) when confined by the basement membrane and **invasive** when it breaches it.

K15.text: **Female sex** and **increasing age** are the strongest risk factors.

K16.text: Hereditary syndromes: **BRCA1** and **BRCA2** mutations, **Li-Fraumeni** syndrome (**TP53**), **Cowden** syndrome (**PTEN**), **Peutz-Jeghers** syndrome (**STK11**), ataxia-telangiectasia (**ATM**), and hereditary diffuse gastric cancer (**CDH1**, linked to lobular carcinoma).

K18.text: Prolonged unopposed oestrogen exposure raises risk: **early menarche**, **late menopause**, **nulliparity**, **first full-term pregnancy after 30**, and not breastfeeding.

K19.text: **Combined hormone replacement therapy**, **postmenopausal obesity**, **alcohol** and **ionising radiation to the chest** (especially in youth, e.g. mantle radiotherapy for Hodgkin lymphoma) increase risk.

K20.text: A personal history of breast cancer, **atypical ductal or lobular hyperplasia** and **LCIS** increase risk; a family history in first-degree relatives increases risk.

K21.text: Breastfeeding and early first full-term pregnancy are protective.

K22.text: **Klinefelter syndrome** and BRCA2 mutation are risk factors for **male breast cancer**, which forms about **1%** of all breast cancers.

K23.text: The **Gail model** estimates a woman's risk of breast cancer from age, reproductive history, biopsies and family history.

K24.text: **DCIS**: malignant cells confined to ducts; the **comedo** (high-grade) type has central necrosis and **calcifies**, so it is usually detected as **microcalcifications on mammography**.

K25.text: **LCIS**: often bilateral and multicentric, does not form a lump or calcify, and is a **risk marker** for invasive cancer in either breast.

K26.text: **Invasive ductal carcinoma (NST)**: the most common type; forms a hard, gritty, stellate mass (**scirrhous** carcinoma).

K27.text: **Invasive lobular carcinoma**: cells in single file (**"Indian file"**) due to loss of **E-cadherin**; more often **bilateral and multicentric**, and spreads unusually to **peritoneum, GI tract, ovaries and meninges**.

K28.text: **Medullary carcinoma**: soft, well-circumscribed, with a prominent **lymphocytic infiltrate**, associated with BRCA1 and triple-negative status.

K29.text: **Mucinous (colloid) carcinoma**: occurs in older women and has a favourable prognosis.

K30.text: **Tubular carcinoma**: well-differentiated and has an excellent prognosis.

K31.text: **Paget's disease of the nipple**: eczematous change of the nipple caused by **Paget cells** (large cells with clear cytoplasm) in the epidermis, almost always with an underlying **DCIS or invasive carcinoma**.

K32.text: Luminal A — ER+ and/or PR+, HER2−, low Ki-67

K33.text: Luminal B — ER+, HER2+ or high Ki-67

K36.text: HER2 is reported **positive** at IHC **3+**; IHC **2+** is equivocal and is resolved by **in situ hybridisation (FISH/ISH)**.

K37.text: Grade uses the **Nottingham (Elston-Ellis) modification of Scarff-Bloom-Richardson**, scoring **tubule formation, nuclear pleomorphism and mitotic count**.

K38.text: **Nottingham Prognostic Index = 0.2 × tumour size (cm) + grade (1–3) + nodal stage (1–3)**.

K39.text: Local spread is along ducts and fascial planes; involvement of **Cooper's (suspensory) ligaments** causes **skin dimpling**, and ductal involvement/fibrosis causes **nipple retraction**.

K40.text: About **75%** of breast lymph drains to the **axillary nodes**; most of the remainder drains to the **internal mammary** nodes.

K41.text: Axillary levels are defined by the **pectoralis minor**: **level I** lateral, **level II** behind (including the interpectoral **Rotter's** nodes), **level III** medial (apical/infraclavicular).

K42.text: **Bone** is the most common site of distant metastasis, mostly **osteolytic**; lung, liver and brain are other common sites.

K43.text: Most commonly a **painless, hard, irregular lump** with ill-defined margins.

K44.text: Skin signs: **dimpling** (Cooper's ligament), **peau d'orange**, ulceration, **satellite skin nodules**, and **cancer en cuirasse** (diffuse infiltration of the chest wall skin).

K45.text: Nipple signs: **recent retraction**, **bloody discharge**, and eczema-like change (Paget's).

K46.text: In Paget's disease the change **starts at the nipple and spreads to the areola**, whereas eczema starts on the areola, is often bilateral and itchy, and spares the nipple.

K47.text: **Fixity to pectoralis major** is tested by examining with the muscle contracted (hands pressed on hips).

K48.text: **Inflammatory carcinoma** presents as a red, warm, swollen breast with peau d'orange involving at least **one-third** of the breast, often without a discrete lump, mimicking mastitis.

K49.text: **Mammography** is the screening tool of choice and the main imaging test in women over about 35–40 years.

K50.text: Mammographic signs of malignancy are a **spiculated (stellate) mass** and **clustered pleomorphic microcalcifications**.

K51.text: **Ultrasound** is preferred in women **under 35** and in dense breasts, and distinguishes solid from cystic lesions.

K52.text: **MRI** is the most sensitive imaging test; it is used for **screening high-risk women (e.g. BRCA carriers)**, assessing **silicone implants**, judging extent of **lobular** carcinoma, and finding the primary in **occult breast cancer** presenting with axillary nodes.

K53.text: **BI-RADS** categories: 0 incomplete, 1 negative, 2 benign, 3 probably benign (short-interval follow-up), 4 suspicious (biopsy), 5 highly suggestive of malignancy, 6 known biopsy-proven malignancy.

K54.text: **Core needle (trucut) biopsy** is the preferred tissue test because it distinguishes invasive from in situ cancer and gives grade and **ER/PR/HER2** status.

K55.text: **Stereotactic or ultrasound-guided** biopsy is used for impalpable lesions such as microcalcifications.

K56.text: FNAC is used mainly for **axillary nodes** and cysts.

K57.text: Routine metastatic work-up is not needed in early asymptomatic disease; it (CT chest/abdomen, bone scan, or PET-CT) is done for locally advanced disease or symptoms.

K58.text: **CA 15-3** and **CEA** are used for monitoring metastatic disease, not for screening or diagnosis.

K59.text: Under India's national NCD programme (NPCDCS / NP-NCD), women aged **30–65** are screened by **clinical breast examination**, rather than population mammography.

K60.text: Tis — DCIS (LCIS was removed from Tis in the 8th edition)

K64.text: T4a — Extension to **chest wall** (ribs, intercostal muscles, serratus anterior; **not pectoralis muscle alone**)

K65.text: T4b — **Skin**: ulceration, ipsilateral satellite nodules, or **peau d'orange**

K68.text: N1 — Mobile ipsilateral level I/II axillary nodes

K69.text: N2a — **Fixed or matted** ipsilateral level I/II axillary nodes

K70.text: N2b — Ipsilateral internal mammary nodes without axillary nodes

K72.text: N3b — Ipsilateral internal mammary **plus** axillary nodes

K74.text: M1 — Distant metastasis (including contralateral axillary/supraclavicular nodes)

K75.text: **Locally advanced breast cancer (LABC)** means stage III disease: tumours > 5 cm with nodes, T4 tumours, or N2/N3 nodal disease.

K76.text: Early breast cancer is treated with **surgery to the breast and axilla**, followed by adjuvant radiotherapy and systemic therapy as indicated by stage and receptor status.

K77.text: **Breast-conserving surgery (BCS)** (wide local excision with clear margins) plus **whole-breast radiotherapy** gives survival **equivalent** to mastectomy in suitable early cancers.

K78.text: For invasive cancer treated with BCS, an adequate margin is **"no ink on tumour"**.

K79.text: **Multicentric disease** (tumours in separate quadrants) or **diffuse malignant-appearing microcalcifications**.

K80.text: **Previous radiotherapy** to the breast or chest wall.

K81.text: **Pregnancy** when radiotherapy would be needed during pregnancy.

K84.text: Relative: a **large tumour relative to breast size** (poor cosmesis) and active **connective tissue disease** (scleroderma, SLE) that increases radiation toxicity.

K85.text: **Halsted radical mastectomy** removes the breast, **pectoralis major and minor**, and all three axillary levels; it is now rarely done.

K86.text: **Modified radical mastectomy (MRM)** removes the breast and axillary nodes while preserving **pectoralis major**.

K87.text: MRM variants: **Patey** (removes pectoralis minor), **Scanlon** (divides pectoralis minor), **Auchincloss** (preserves pectoralis minor and clears levels I–II).

K88.text: Reconstruction options include implants, the **latissimus dorsi flap**, the pedicled **TRAM flap** (based on the **superior epigastric** vessels), and the free **DIEP flap**.

K89.text: **Sentinel lymph node biopsy (SLNB)** is the standard axillary staging for **clinically node-negative** invasive cancer, using **radioisotope (Tc-99m sulphur colloid)** and/or **blue dye** (isosulfan blue / methylene blue).

K90.text: SLNB is **contraindicated** in **inflammatory breast cancer** and in **biopsy-proven node-positive** axilla, where axillary lymph node dissection (ALND) is done.

K91.text: After the **ACOSOG Z0011** trial, women with **1–2 positive sentinel nodes** treated with BCS and whole-breast radiotherapy can **omit ALND**.

K92.text: Standard ALND clears **levels I and II**.

K94.text: **Post-mastectomy radiotherapy** is indicated for **≥ 4 positive nodes**, **T3/T4** tumours and **positive margins**, and is considered for 1–3 positive nodes.

K95.text: **Neoadjuvant chemotherapy** is used for **LABC** and **inflammatory** cancer, and to downstage operable tumours to allow BCS.

K97.text: **Tamoxifen** (a SERM) for **5–10 years** is used for hormone-receptor-positive **premenopausal** women.

K98.text: **Aromatase inhibitors** are preferred for hormone-receptor-positive **postmenopausal** women, because postmenopausal oestrogen comes from peripheral aromatisation.

K99.text: Tamoxifen side effects: **endometrial carcinoma**, **thromboembolism (DVT/PE)**, hot flushes and **cataract**.

K101.text: **Trastuzumab** (anti-HER2 monoclonal antibody) is given for **1 year** in HER2-positive disease; its cardiotoxicity is usually **reversible and not dose-related**, unlike the **dose-dependent** cardiomyopathy of **anthracyclines (doxorubicin)**.

K102.text: Gene-expression assays such as **Oncotype DX (21-gene recurrence score)** guide whether ER-positive, HER2-negative early cancers need chemotherapy.

K103.text: **DCIS**: treated with **BCS + radiotherapy** or **mastectomy**; routine ALND is not done, and **SLNB is done if mastectomy** is performed.

K104.text: **Classic LCIS**: managed with **surveillance** and consideration of **chemoprevention**, not mastectomy.

K105.text: **Paget's disease**: treated according to the underlying cancer, by mastectomy or central BCS (excision of nipple-areola complex) with radiotherapy.

K107.text: **Pregnancy-associated breast cancer**: **MRM** is preferred in the first trimester; chemotherapy is safe in the **second and third trimesters**; **radiotherapy, tamoxifen and trastuzumab are avoided** during pregnancy.

K108.text: **Male breast cancer**: usually treated by **mastectomy with axillary staging**; most are hormone-receptor-positive and receive **tamoxifen**.

K109.text: **Metastatic disease**: treated primarily with systemic therapy (endocrine first-line if hormone-receptor-positive without visceral crisis), with **bisphosphonates or denosumab** for bone metastases.

K110.text: **Chemoprevention** uses **tamoxifen**, **raloxifene** (postmenopausal; no increase in endometrial cancer) or aromatase inhibitors.

K111.text: **Bilateral risk-reducing mastectomy** in BRCA carriers reduces breast cancer risk by about **90%**.

K112.text: Of axillary dissection: **lymphoedema of the arm**, seroma, shoulder stiffness, and nerve injury.

K113.text: **Intercostobrachial nerve** injury → numbness of the medial upper arm/axilla.

K114.text: **Long thoracic nerve (of Bell)** injury → paralysis of **serratus anterior** → **winging of the scapula**.

K116.text: **Stewart-Treves syndrome** is **lymphangiosarcoma** arising in a chronically lymphoedematous arm after mastectomy/ALND.

K117.text: **Seroma** is the most common early complication after mastectomy.

K136.text: PYQs have expected **carcinoma cervix** as the most common cancer in Indian women; breast cancer has since overtaken it and is now the most common.

K137.text: PYQs have expected **FNAC** as the investigation of choice for a breast lump; current practice is **core needle biopsy**, which gives histology and receptor status.

K138.text: Older classifications and PYQs counted **supraclavicular nodes** as **M1**; current AJCC staging places them in **N3c**.

K139.text: Older keys gave **radical (Halsted) mastectomy** for operable cancer; current practice is **BCS + radiotherapy** or **MRM**.

K140.text: Exam trap: **peau d'orange** is **T4b**, not T4d; **T4d** needs the clinical picture of inflammatory carcinoma.

K141.text: Exam trap: invasion of **pectoralis major alone** is **not T4a** chest-wall involvement.

K142.text: Exam trap: the cardiotoxicity of **trastuzumab** is reversible and not dose-dependent, while that of **doxorubicin** is dose-dependent and largely irreversible.

K143.text: Exam trap: **tamoxifen** raises the risk of endometrial cancer, but **raloxifene** does not.

K144.text: Exam trap: the **most common cause of bloody nipple discharge** is **intraductal papilloma**, not carcinoma.
